name: Azure Spot VM: 30-second eviction notice, mandatory USD max price, and disk billing that follows the eviction policy
region: all Azure regions except Azure operated by 21Vianet
price_basis: SECONDS OF WARNING, not a price. Azure's documentation: 'Azure will evict Azure Spot Virtual Machines with 30-seconds notice' and these are 'delivered on a best effort basis up to 30 seconds prior to the eviction'. price_usd carries the 30 (seconds). The concrete anchor is the existing eastus ND96isr H100 v5 record at $2.2712 per H100-hour spot against $12.29 on-demand - about 82% off, the deepest hyperscaler spot discount on Hopper in this slice. OBSERVATION DATE: the figure above was observed/listed on 2026-10-04 unless a different date is stated inline; treat it as needing re-verification once it is more than a quarter old. PRICE CLASS: this is a PUBLISHED LIST PRICE - an asking rate a new customer is quoted, not a realised, discounted or negotiated transaction rate. A real bill is at or below this and typically well below it once commitments, credits and committed-use discounts are applied.
notes:
Azure's spot mechanism has three properties that change a cost model rather than just discounting it. (1) YOU MUST SET A MAX PRICE, in US dollars, 'using up to five decimal places' (e.g. 0.98765 means $0.98765/hour). If your max price is below the current spot price the VM is not deployed at all; if spot rises above your max, the VM is evicted and will NOT automatically restart even after the price falls back. A max price of -1 means never evict for price, and you are then charged the lesser of spot or the standard on-demand price - so -1 is a useful floor-setting trick, not an unlimited bid. (2) EVICTION POLICY IS A BILLING DECISION: Deallocate (default) keeps the disks and you keep paying for them; Delete removes the VM 'together with their underlying disks, so you'll not continue to be charged for the storage'. For an inference box with a 28,000 GiB temp store this is a material ongoing charge, not a rounding error. (3) NO SLA and NO HIGH AVAILABILITY GUARANTEE, stated plainly: 'there's no SLA for these VMs'. Azure is also the only major cloud publishing per-SKU spot EVICTION RATES - 'Eviction rates are quoted per hour. For example, an eviction rate of 10% means a VM has a 10% chance of being evicted within the next hour, based on historical eviction data of the last 7 days' - queryable for the last 28 trailing days via Azure Resource Graph's SpotResources table along with 90 days of spot price history. That is the best interruption data any of the three clouds publishes, and it means an Azure spot buyer can actually measure their own risk instead of guessing. Note also: the Spot flag is only settable at creation and Spot VMs cannot be converted to Standard, so there is no downgrade path.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; sources spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance, spl-bis-2026-01-advanced-computing-case-by-case): renting capacity does NOT remove the export-control question, it relocates it. Providing remote access to controlled computing capability can constitute a transfer under the EAR, so the provider must screen the end user; and separately, under the 91 FR 1684 licence regime the consignee must run KYC procedures to prevent unauthorized remote access and must manage and limit IaaS access to the hardware - obligations pushed onto the customer, who must be told to implement them. For a customer headquartered or parented in Country Group D:5 or Macau the 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) end-user/parent test can bite even when the capacity is consumed in a permitted region. Recorded true because the underlying hardware is controlled and the provider carries the screening duty, not because access to a US region is itself restricted.

 LEAD TIME: null - correct and not a gap. A token-priced serverless API is provisioned on request, so there is no lead time to publish; the binding constraint when a model is at capacity is provider-side queuing and any per-account concurrency limit, which this repo records in notes where a vendor publishes one (see the DeepSeek concurrency figures already here). Deliberately NOT recorded: any 'model capacity lead time' estimate, because vendors publish none and the SEO 'GPU lead time' numbers that circulate do not apply to a rented endpoint. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.
